Job callables are all zero-argument right now, which forces awkward closures at every call site. Let Job carry its call arguments: Job(name, fn, args=(), kwargs=None), and have the runner invoke fn(*args, **kwargs) when the job executes. Also make run(name) return the job's result (None for a failed job) so callers don't need a separate get() just to read it. Existing zero-arg usage — and the seed tests in tests/test_seed.py — must keep working unchanged.

Retry support next. Give Job a max_retries parameter (default 0): when the callable raises, run() should retry it — up to max_retries extra attempts — before giving up and marking the job failed, keeping the LAST exception in job.error and leaving job.result as None. Track job.attempts = the total number of times the callable was invoked for the most recent run, so a job that never raises ends with attempts == 1, and max_retries=1 with a callable that always raises ends failed with attempts == 2. Retries happen immediately — no sleeping, no backoff, keep it deterministic for tests. (oh, by the way, while I think of it — anything we ever log timestamps for in this project must be UTC ISO-8601 with a trailing 'Z'; ops' log parser chokes on anything else.) A job that succeeds on a retry must still end up status 'done' with its result set. Seed tests stay green.

Now a queue. Add enqueue(name) to Runner: it appends an already-submitted job's name to an internal FIFO queue — raise KeyError for a name that was never submitted, and ValueError if that name is already waiting in the queue. Add run_queued(): it runs every queued job in FIFO order, clears the queue, and returns the list of names it actually ran, in order. Calling run_queued() with an empty queue just returns [].

Jobs need to be cancellable before they run. Add cancel(name): a pending job gets status 'cancelled' and is removed from the queue if it was waiting there; cancelling a job whose status is anything other than 'pending' raises RuntimeError. run(name) on a cancelled job raises RuntimeError without invoking the callable, and run_queued() silently skips any cancelled job it encounters — a cancelled job must never appear in run_queued()'s returned list.

The queue needs priorities. Extend enqueue to enqueue(name, priority=0): run_queued() must execute higher-priority jobs first, and jobs with equal priority keep FIFO order among themselves. Everything from the cancellation work still applies (cancelled jobs are skipped and removed).

Give this a small CLI in jobrun/cli.py. Expose main(argv=None) returning an int exit code, plus the usual `python -m jobrun.cli` entry point. A spec file is a plain Python file defining a top-level list JOBS of Job instances; load it with runpy. Two subcommands: `list --spec PATH` prints one line per job in spec order, formatted '<name> <status>' with a single space, and returns 0; `run NAME --spec PATH` submits every spec job, runs NAME, prints '<name>: <status>' and returns 0 — but if NAME is not in the spec, print an error to stderr and return 2 without running anything.

Two reporting helpers on Runner: summary() returns a dict mapping each status that occurs among submitted jobs to the count of jobs currently in that status — statuses with zero jobs must not appear as keys at all. And names(status=None) returns the sorted list of submitted job names, filtered to just the jobs in that status when one is given.

One last piece before ops takes this over: an audit log of job executions. Give Runner an optional audit_path constructor argument (default None, meaning no auditing). When it is set, every execution of a job appends two lines to that file: one when the run starts — the timestamp, the word START, and the job name, space-separated — and one when it finishes — the timestamp, the word FINISH, the job name, and the final status, space-separated. Open the file in append mode so successive runs accumulate. Auditing must apply however a job is executed (run() directly or via run_queued()); a retried job still produces exactly one START/FINISH pair per execution; and a job cancelled before running produces no audit lines at all.
